clue.text: Listen cryptically getting the cold shoulder

indicators.note: treating a word cryptically means playing with it, here by jumbling its letters into another word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the clue itself describes what has been done to the word: it has been given a cryptic treatment

explanation.surface: Someone tries to listen but is being ignored by everyone around them.
explanation.walkthrough: SILENT is LISTEN jumbled, and the setter names the operation itself as the second word: the clue describes a SILENT TREATMENT of the word listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms describe deliberately ignoring a person, refusing to speak to them as a snub.

clue.text: Looking up to notice on motorway telephone

blocks.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
the M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, written with I for the digit 1
to ring someone is to telephone them

explanation.surface: Someone spots a sign about phoning while driving on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up to someone is to respect and esteem them, which is what admiring means.

clue.text: Step outside parts of Paris, France

indicators.note: the outside parts of a phrase are its two ends, so letters come from the front and the back

blocks.note: the two letters at each end of the phrase read as one run

explanation.surface: An invitation to stroll around the outskirts of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'outside parts' takes two letters from each end of the whole phrase, not one: PA from the front, CE from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace is a single stride taken while walking, so the noun step is a synonym.

clue.text: Row of churchwardens bearing oil here?

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: where oil is carried

blocks.note: a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe
a row of things is a line of them

explanation.surface: A row of parish officials carrying oil, perhaps for the church lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchwardens look like church officials but are long clay pipes; a row of pipes laid end to end is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is transported over long distances through a long conduit of joined tubes.

clue.text: Quick drawing of small sailing boat

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An artist dashes off a picture of a little yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough, rapidly made picture, done before or instead of a finished work.

clue.text: King in glasses waves

indicators.note: a king in something is placed inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: beakers are drinking glasses or cups
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wearing spectacles waves to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' suggests spectacles and 'waves' a royal greeting; in fact glasses are drinking vessels and waves the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakers are large sea waves that crash into foam on the shore.

clue.text: Fit brief

blocks.note: first meaning: in good condition, as an athlete is (two words
second meaning: to tell someone the facts, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer is an adjective phrase for fitness; read as one word it is a verb for giving information.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsperson playing well is said to be in good shape; to brief someone is to tell them what they need to know.

clue.text: Actors marry dons around Highland county

indicators.note: letters moved around are put into a different order

blocks.note: every letter of the three words is used

explanation.surface: Performers wed university teachers somewhere in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty is a former county in the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a historic administrative county in the Scottish Highlands, spanning the north-west mainland and Lewis.

clue.text: Calligraphy item in kind, in a novel

indicators.note: something novel is new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these three short words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A calligrapher's supply described as appearing in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In kind' looks like the phrase meaning payment in goods; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian ink is a dense black ink used by calligraphers and artists for pen work.

clue.text: Leading recitalist performing party piece

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is the one at its front

blocks.note: the first letter
a performer on stage is on
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A star soloist plays a showpiece at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party piece' reads as one phrase for a favourite turn; it splits so that party gives letters and piece is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical composition with a recurring main theme, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: In English wood, church camp

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it, here a word placed within a pair of words

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
pine is a type of wood
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church group camping in an English forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' suggests a tent site but is the adjective for theatrical, effeminate behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene describes something effeminate or sexually ambiguous, matching the adjective camp in its flamboyant sense.

clue.text: Leaves in hot water here?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone abandons a person in trouble
setter's reading: the place where tea leaves steep in boiling water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb and 'in hot water' an idiom for trouble; read literally they are tea leaves brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels for brewing tea hold the dried leaves while they infuse in boiling water.

clue.text: Neat cut

blocks.note: first meaning: tidy and well kept, an adjective
second meaning: to shorten slightly, or the act of doing so

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a haircut, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy, smart appearance is described with this adjective; as a verb it means clipping a little off.

clue.text: Docker who has dieted?

blocks.note: setter's reading: a worker in the docks who moves cargo by barge
surface reading: someone who has lost weight is now less heavy

explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to ferry goods to and from ships, so its worker is a lighterman; split, it is a man weighing less.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighterman operates barges in a port, loading and unloading ships, so he is a dock worker.

clue.text: Dressage music

blocks.note: rags, as in glad rags, is slang for clothes, so to rag is to dress
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The soundtrack played during a horse-riding display.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressage, horse training shown in competition, must be split into two words, dress and age.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated style of piano music popular in America around 1900.

clue.text: Incorporated paramour on easy street

blocks.note: Inc is the abbreviation for Incorporated, used for companies
a paramour is an illicit lover

explanation.surface: A company's secret lover living a life of luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms describe living comfortably and prosperously without worries about money.

clue.text: As nice as Ritz’s top cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, for mixing
the first letter of the hotel's name

explanation.surface: A drink praised as being as good as the best served at the Ritz hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'As' looks like part of the comparison 'as nice as'; it is the definition, the chemical symbol, while the second 'as' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the element arsenic on the periodic table.

clue.text: Cohort having trouble around middle of field on horseback

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter
one thing placed around another encloses it

blocks.note: aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble
the central letter of the five
a jockey riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: A band of riders causing trouble in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang for violent trouble or aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort in statistics is a set of people born in the same period, i.e. of similar years.

clue.text: Everyone knows feature is on island, out East

indicators.note: something out is gone, so the letter named is removed

blocks.note: the nose is a facial feature
Crete is a Greek island
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A well-known feature of a Mediterranean island lies out to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E is the one dropped from the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is common knowledge, people say it is no secret: nothing is hidden about it.

clue.text: Large lorry blocks topped vegetables

indicators.note: a thing that is topped has had its head cut off, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a big British truck
to choke a pipe is to block it

explanation.surface: A big truck blocks the road and crushes a load of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped vegetables' looks like one phrase, but topped applies only to blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Globe artichokes are thistle-like plants whose flower buds are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Dress code first introduced in capital

definitions.note: singular noun for a plural answer, or verb-ish; read as items of dress

indicators.note: the first of a word is the letter it starts with
something introduced into another goes inside it

blocks.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A capital city brings in a new dress code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress code' reads as one phrase; it splits so that dress is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunics are loose garments, so they count as dress in the sense of clothing.

clue.text: Writer invested in dictionary as on first night?

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: what a show did on its first night

indicators.note: to be invested in is to be clothed within, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author has money in a dictionary project that launches like a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' suggests money; here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or show begins its run on its first night, so it started then.

clue.text: Some school’s outing returning to capital

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters is used
returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A school trip heads home to a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian seat of government, it is a capital city in Scandinavia.

clue.text: Carriageway cover on isle’s complete, we’re told

indicators.note: what we are told we hear spoken, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
complete means entire; the word sounds like an opening

explanation.surface: Roadworks on an island have been finished, so locals report.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhole has an iron lid set into the road surface, covering access to drains.

clue.text: Novel medieval instrument starts to come apart

indicators.note: the starts of words are their initial letters

blocks.note: a rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument
the initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An old musical instrument, newly made, begins falling to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, or an anagram signal; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's famous 1938 book, a gothic romance.

clue.text: Call corporation endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, a big stomach

explanation.surface: Someone phones a company over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation looks like a business; it is a jocular old word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them, so call in the telephone sense.

clue.text: Gem with inlay carved evenly

indicators.note: evenly means taking the letters in even-numbered positions

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A jewel set into a carved, inlaid surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, mother-of-pearl, is the iridescent lining of shells and is used like a precious stone in jewellery.

clue.text: Agitated farm animal that is caught in snarled net

indicators.note: something caught in a net is held inside it
a snarled net is tangled, so its letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: a bull is a male farm animal
ie is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: An angry bull thrashes about, tangled in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' looks like an anagram signal describing the animal; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient literally means boiling over, describing someone bubbling with excitement and energy.
